title: INITIATIVES FOR PROMOTION OF AYUSH
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Ayush has launched several initiatives to promote the production, quality, research, marketing and Global acceptance of Ayush medicines. The major initiatives include:
Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY): Supports quality assurance, standardization, Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), testing infrastructure, pharmacopoeial standards and capacity building of the Ayush drug sector.
AYURGYAN Scheme: Promotes evidence-based research, innovation, clinical studies and higher education in Ayush systems.
Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H): Development and publication of pharmacopoeial standards, formularies and quality standards for Ayush drugs.
International Cooperation Scheme (IC Scheme): Supports Indian Ayush drug Manufacturers/ Ayush Service providers to boost the export of Ayush products and services; facilitates the International promotion, development and recognition of Ayush systems of medicine; foster interaction of stakeholders and market development of Ayush at international level; promote academics and research through the establishment of Ayush Academic Chairs in foreign countries and holding training workshop/symposiums for promoting and strengthening awareness and interest about Ayush systems of Medicine at International level.
Ayush Export Promotion Council (Ayushexcil): Facilitates export of Ayush products and services by supporting exporters through International exhibitions, seminars, buyer-seller meets, and capacity building of manufacturers and service providers.
Ministry of Ayush is implementing a Central Sector Scheme, namely, Ayush Oushadhi Gunvatta Evam Uttpadan Samvardhan Yojana (AOGUSY) to support Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards like WHO Good Manufacturing Practices (WHO-GMP) and National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) respectively. The components of scheme are as follows: -
Strengthening and up-gradation of Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories to achieve higher standards.
Pharmacovigilance of ASU&H drugs including surveillance of misleading advertisements.
Strengthening of Central and State regulatory frameworks including Technical Human Resource & Capacity Building programs for Ayush drugs.
Support for development of standards and accreditation/certification of Ayush products & materials in collaboration with Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Quality Control of India (QCI) and other relevant scientific institutions and industrial R&D centers.
The details of financial assistance provided to Ayush Pharmacies and Drug Testing Laboratories including MSMEs during the last three years, State-wise including Karnataka is furnished at annexure-I.
Following steps have been taken by the Ministry to strengthen quality control, standardisation, pharmacovigilance and export of Ayush medicines-
The Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Drugs Rules, 1945 have exclusive regulatory provisions for Ayush drugs. It is mandatory for the manufacturers to adhere to the prescribed requirements for licensing of manufacturing units & medicines including proof of safety & effectiveness, compliance with the Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) as per Schedule T and Schedule M-I of the Drugs Rules, 1945 for Ayurvedic, Siddha, Sowa-rigpa, Unani and Homeopathy drugs respectively and to follow the quality standards of drugs as prescribed in the respective pharmacopoeia. Drug Testing Laboratories are approved by the Ministry of Ayush under Rules 160A to 160J of the Drugs Rules, 1945, for carrying out tests relating to the identity, purity, quality and strength of Ayush drugs. As on date, 118 private Drug Testing Laboratories have been approved by the Ministry across States and Union Territories for conducting such tests in accordance with the provisions of the Drugs Rules, 1945.
Drug Inspectors collect medicine samples regularly from manufacturing firms or retail shops within their jurisdiction and send them to Drug Testing Laboratory under Drug Control department for quality testing and if any sample is found to be ‘Not of Standard Quality’, appropriate action is initiated such as preventing the sale of the medicines from the market and appropriate legal actions as per Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules made thereunder. There are 34 Drug Testing Laboratories available in State/UTs for testing of the Legal Samples drawn by the Drug Inspectors of concerned State/UTs.
The Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine & Homoeopathy (PCIM&H), a subordinate organization under Ministry of Ayush, develops pharmacopoeial standards and formulary specifications for Ayush drugs, which serve as the official compendia for determining their identity, purity, and strength. Compliance with these standards is mandatory under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder. PCIM&H also functions as the Appellate Drug Testing Laboratory for Ayush drugs and conducts regular capacity-building programmes for Drug Regulatory Authorities, Drug Analysts, and other stakeholders on standardization, quality control, and testing methodologies to strengthen the quality assurance system for Ayush drugs.
The Pharmacovigilance Program for Ayush drugs under AOGUSY scheme functions through a nationwide three-tier network comprising 01 National Pharmacovigilance Co-ordination Centre (NPvCC), 05 Intermediary Pharmacovigilance Centres (IPvCs), and 97 Peripheral Pharmacovigilance Centres (PPvCs) established across the country. These centres are mandated to monitor suspected adverse drug reactions and report the misleading advertisements to the respective State Regulatory Authorities for suitable action against the defaulter(s). Further, through this program various stakeholders across the country are sensitised towards the quality of medicines, posologies and other drug-related issues. To strengthen the pharmacovigilance system for Ayush drugs, Ministry of Ayush has launched an IT enabled online portal “Ayush Suraksha” on 30th May 2025 to capture MLAs/OAs and report suspected Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) related to the Ayush medicine.
Further, Ministry of Ayush has undertaken the following initiatives to promote quality assurance and certification of Ayush products in order to promote export of Ayush medicines.
WHO Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (WHO-CoPP) to Ayush drugs is issued by Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) after joint inspections of manufacturing units by Drug Inspectors posted in Ayush vertical along with drug inspectors of State/UTs and CDSCO for compliance with WHO Technical Report Series (TRS) guidelines for Herbal Medicines.
Ministry of Ayush has launched Ayush Quality Mark (AQM) initiative through the Ayush Export Promotion Council (AYUSHEXCIL). Under this framework, the Ayush Quality Mark is being granted after scrutiny and verification of valid quality certifications and statutory approvals issued by the competent Government authorities, such as WHO-GMP, Ayush Premium Mark and other recognised certifications, as applicable.
The Ministry of Ayush has taken the following measures to increase the availability of certified Ayush medicines and public awareness across the country;
Under centrally sponsored scheme of National Ayush Mission, State/UT Governments are being supported for supply of essentials Ayush medicines for Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) and Government Ayush hospitals/dispensaries as per the proposal received in their State Annual Action Plan (SAAP).
The Ayush Export Promotion Council (AYUSHEXCIL), notified by Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Ministry of Commerce and supported by Ministry of Ayush, has signed Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) with quick-commerce platform Zepto on January 28, 2026, and the Spice Board of India on May 25, 2026, to promote digital domestic delivery and boosting International exports of Ayush Medicines respectively.
Public awareness initiatives through Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns, observance of International Day of Yoga, Ayurveda Day, Social Media campaign  and other outreach programmes like national and international exhibitions, fairs and conferences etc.

title: Sowa-Rigpa Must Emerge as a Globally Recognised Evidence-Based Healthcare System: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav
subtitle:
National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR) Should Become a Global Centre for Holistic Wellness: Shri Prataprao Jadhav

Union Ayush Minister Chairs 2nd Governing Body Meeting of the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, chaired the 2nd Governing Body Meeting of the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR) in New Delhi and outlined a strategic roadmap for strengthening Sowa-Rigpa through scientific research, academic excellence, institutional development and expansion across the Indian Himalayan Region (IHR).
Setting out the Institute's priorities for the coming years, the Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav emphasised that the next phase of growth should focus on strengthening scientific research, promoting international standards and expanding the reach of Sowa-Rigpa beyond its traditional geographical boundaries.
Addressing the Governing Body, Shri Prataprao Jadhav said, "Our goal is no longer limited to developing infrastructure; it is to establish Sowa-Rigpa as a mainstream healthcare system in India and across the world. Our foremost commitment is to establish Sowa-Rigpa as an evidence-based system of medical science before the world. To achieve this, we must accelerate our research strategies, and the establishment of an independent research council will be the first important step. We must build an ecosystem that integrates traditional wisdom with scientific excellence through evidence-based research, strong academic institutions and globally accepted standards."
Shri Prataprao Jadhav further said, "I firmly believe that the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa is not merely an institution of Ladakh; it is the custodian of the medical heritage of the entire Indian Himalayan Region. We must strengthen both of its regional models and deepen our engagement with the Himalayan communities. Greater focus should be given to sustainable cultivation of rare medicinal plants, bio-prospecting, agroforestry and conservation of medicinal biodiversity so that local communities become equal partners in preserving and promoting this invaluable knowledge system. Together, let us transform this institution into a global centre for holistic wellness."
Shri Jadhav suggested that hundreds of Bhoti language manuscripts containing the invaluable knowledge and heritage of Sowa-Rigpa should be preserved through systematic transcription and translation. He proposed that, as a first step, these manuscripts be digitised, followed by their translation to make this rich repository of knowledge accessible to the general public and researchers. He further proposed that the digitisation drive be accelerated with the work being undertaken by NISR, the Gyan Bharatam Mission or any other competent institution, and, if required, through collaboration with the Ministry of Culture. He emphasised that preserving and digitising this invaluable knowledge is essential for safeguarding India's traditional medical heritage and strengthening future research in Sowa-Rigpa.
Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, said that the Ministry is committed to building strong institutions that preserve India's traditional medical knowledge while advancing it through modern scientific approaches. He noted that NISR has emerged as a key institution for promoting Sowa-Rigpa through quality education, clinical services, research and capacity building, and reaffirmed the Ministry's continued support for its long-term development.
The Governing Body also congratulated Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director, National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa, on being conferred the Padma Shri in 2026 in recognition of his outstanding contributions to the field of medicine, particularly for his pioneering efforts in reviving, preserving and institutionalising the ancient Sowa-Rigpa system of medicine in India. The members appreciated his leadership in advancing Sowa-Rigpa through education, research, clinical services and institutional development.
Dr. Padma Gurmet presented the Institute's progress and future action plan before the Governing Body. He highlighted achievements in academics, clinical services, research, medicinal plant conservation and outreach programmes, while outlining proposals aimed at further strengthening institutional capacity and expanding the reach of Sowa-Rigpa across the country.
Sowa-Rigpa, meaning "Knowledge of Healing" in the Bhoti language, is one of the world's oldest traditional systems of medicine and has been recognised by the Government of India under the Ayush framework. Popularly known as the Amchi system of medicine, it is practised across the Indian Himalayan Region and several neighbouring countries. Over centuries, the system evolved and flourished across the Trans-Himalayan region and today represents a rich repository of traditional medical knowledge.
The Governing Body deliberated on key policy, academic and research initiatives aimed at strengthening the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa as the apex institution for education, research and healthcare in Sowa-Rigpa. The Ministry of Ayush reaffirmed its commitment to advancing this ancient Himalayan medical tradition through scientific validation, institutional excellence and wider public outreach.

title: AGRICULTURAL YIELD LOSSES DUE TO HUMAN-INDUCED LAND DEGRADATION
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Government has not undertaken any assessment on agricultural land affected by degradation and its impact on crop productivity. However, as per Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of India (2021) published by the Space Applications Centre (ISRO), an area of 6.38 lakh ha is manmade desertification and land degradation in the country as on 2018–19. The State wise details, including the State of Maharashtra, are given in Annexure.
The Government has taken various measures to promote soil restoration, sustainable land management, water conservation and climate resilient agriculture to improve agricultural productivity, as given below:
Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) reported that, to promote soil restoration and sustainable land management, it has developed and recommended location-specific technologies such as contour cultivation, intercropping, crop rotation, conservation agriculture, mulching, green manuring, reduced tillage, agroforestry etc. For the management of salt-affected soils, ICAR recommends gypsum application, bio-drainage, subsurface drainage, salt-tolerant crop varieties and bio-reclamation measures, including salt-tolerant grasses. ICAR has also developed General Fertilizer Recommendations (GFR) and Soil Test Crop Response (STCR)-based recommendations, which have been shared with the States to promote soil test-based balanced nutrient application, improve soil fertility, enhance soil organic carbon and increase nutrient-use efficiency. For water conservation, ICAR promotes integrated watershed management through bio-engineering measures, contour and graded bunds, stone bunds, contour and staggered trenches, bench terraces, check dams and water harvesting structures such as farm ponds and community ponds.
Further, The Government through, Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) is implementing a project- National Innovations in Climate Resilient Agriculture (NICRA) in 651 districts that studies the impact of climate change on agriculture and conducts district level risk & vulnerability assessment due to climate change. Out of the 310 districts identified as vulnerable to climate change, 201 have been categorized as 'High' climate-vulnerable and 109 as 'Very High' climate-vulnerable. District Agriculture Contingency Plans (DACPs) for these 651 districts have also been prepared to address weather aberrations and recommending location specific climate resilient crops and varieties and management practices. To enhance resilience to climate variability, location-specific climate-resilient technologies, including the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), aerobic rice, direct-seeded rice and in-situ crop residue management, are being demonstrated for adoption by farmers. Under NICRA, climate-resilient technologies are being demonstrated in 448 Climate Resilient Villages across 151 vulnerable districts in 28 States/UTs, supported by village-level seed banks and community nurseries to enhance farmers' resilience and ensure timely availability of quality seeds. Technical assistance is provided to small and marginal farmers through Village Climate Risk Management Committees (VCRMCs), while training programmes are conducted under the Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA). Further, ICAR has released 2900 varieties during last 10 years (2014-2024), out of which 2661 varieties are tolerant to one or more biotic and/or abiotic stresses.
The Government is implementing various programmes to promote sustainable and climate-resilient agricultural practices to reverse yield losses and improve agricultural productivity. Per Drop More Crop scheme is implemented to promote water use efficiency at the farm level through Micro Irrigation technologies i.e. drip and sprinkler irrigation systems. Rainfed Area Development scheme is implemented to promote Integrated Farming System for enhancing productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic variability. The Soil Health and Fertility scheme assists states in promoting Integrated Nutrient Management through judicious use of fertilizers. The Government is also promoting organic farming through Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana and natural farming through National Mission on Natural Farming scheme. “Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses”, National Mission on Edible Oils – Oilseeds, and National Food Security & Nutrition Mission promotes crop diversification.  Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture, Agroforestry & National Bamboo Mission also promote climate resilience in agriculture. Further, Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana along with weather index based Restructured Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme provides a comprehensive insurance cover against failure of the crops, thereby helping compensate farmers for losses caused by natural calamities and climate-related risks.
Under Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission – Gramin (VB-G RAM-G), water conservation activities are prioritised through Natural Resource Management (NRM) works. These constitutes 110 works out of 318 permissible works under the programme that improves water security and conservation. Further, the Watershed Management (WM) Division of the Department of Land Resources (DoLR) implements the Watershed Development Component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-PMKSY) for the development of rainfed and degraded lands across the country. The activities undertaken, inter alia, include ridge area treatment, drainage line treatment, soil and moisture conservation, rainwater harvesting, nursery raising, pasture development, and livelihood support for asset-less persons. Through these interventions, WDC-PMKSY seeks to promote sustainable development by improving natural resource management and enhancing the resilience of farmers to climate change.
Despite the challenges posed by biotic and abiotic stresses, the agriculture sector has recorded sustained growth in crop productivity and overall agricultural production over the last decade. Food grain production has increased from 252.03 million tonnes in 2014–15 to a record 357.73 million tonnes in 2024–25, while horticulture production has increased from 280.98 million tonnes in 2014–15 to 370.73 million tonnes in 2024–25, reflecting the resilience and steady growth of agricultural production across the country.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF AGRISTACK AND DIGITAL AGRICULTURE MISSION
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
AgriStack is the farmer-centric Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) built as a public good for efficient, easier and faster service and scheme delivery to the farmers. It provides a comprehensive profile of every farmer, such as farmer’s details, land records, crops grown, and assets such as livestock and fisheries. It consists of three foundational registries associated with the agriculture sector, i.e., Farmer Registry, Geo-Referenced Village Maps and Crop Sown Registry, all created and maintained by the State Governments/ Union Territories. The Farmer Registry created under AgriStack is designed to serve as a foundational database for the efficient, transparent and faster delivery of agricultural services. Farmer Registry is being integrated with various farmer-centric schemes services and digital platforms to
expedite credit disbursements, access to crop insurance
, weather advisories, MSP-based crop procurement systems etc.
Farmer ID is created by synchronizing farmers' details with their digitized land records. As of 3rd August, 2026, more than 10.31 Crore Farmer IDs have been created across the country. Further, during Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was conducted in 648 Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the country. Manipur has initiated the process of DCS and participating in the process of creation of Farmer ID.
The State Farmer Registry is built in a federated manner, which means the ownership of the data is with the respective States. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has developed the AgriStack in accordance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules 2025, to ensure the complete privacy of farmers' data by ensuring that farmers' data is collected only with their consent and farmers have full control over their data for sharing with authorized entities for specific purposes. Further, the security features of AgriStack are fully compliant with the cybersecurity guidelines of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In). AgriStack maintains farmers' information in an encrypted manner so that only the authorized systems can read it.
Under the YES-TECH initiative of the Crop Insurance Scheme, technology-based yield estimation is being implemented for Paddy, Wheat, and Soybean crops. Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning (ML) is one of the approach identified for crop yield estimation under this initiative.
For crop yield estimation, a digital initiative, Digital General Crop Estimation System (DGCES) has been developed, which provides accurate and timely crop yield data for crop production estimates.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR
in a written reply in Rajya  Sabha today.

10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) have been formed under the Central Sector Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs).
1,175 FPOs have been set up under the scheme with 100% women members. Of the total shareholders across FPOs, about 40% are women.  The scheme mandates that the Board of Directors or the Governing Body in each FPO should have minimum one woman member.
FPOs formed are operational and are engaged in activities such as input supply, aggregation, procurement, value addition and marketing of agricultural produce. 9865 FPOs have taken Management cost, 8357 FPOs have taken Equity Grant and 3140 FPOs have taken Credit Guarantee.  Under the Scheme, each FPO is provided professional handholding support for a period of five years from the date of its registration through the designated Implementing Agencies. When an FPO exhibits low levels of activity, the Implementing Agency, through the CBBO, provides appropriate handholding, capacity building, business facilitation and market linkage support to improve its functioning and promote long-term sustainability.
The FPOs have been formed in different years since 2020-21 and are at different stages of development and business operations. Accordingly, their turnover varies, depending on the period of operation and the scale of business activities. The cumulative turnover reported by the FPOs formed under the Central Sector Scheme is ₹20,358 crore as on 31st July, 2026.

title: Implementaiton of National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government has approved the National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP) as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme with the objective of increasing the area and productivity of oil palm and thereby enhancing domestic production of edible oils and reducing dependence on imports. The Mission was launched in 2021-22 with a financial outlay of Rs. 11,040 crore, including a Government of India share of Rs. 8,844 crore, and a target of bringing 6.5 lakh hectares under oil palm cultivation during 2021-22 to 2025-26.
The Mission is being implemented in 15 States, (Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Karnataka, Kerala, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Tripura). The major interventions under NMEO-OP include assistance for planting material, maintenance of plantations, intercropping, drip irrigation, farm machinery, replanting, establishment of seed gardens and nurseries, and development of oil palm processing infrastructure, besides a price assurance mechanism for farmers through the Viability Gap Payment (VGP).
During 2021-22 to 2025-26, a total area of 2.73 lakh hectares was brought under oil palm cultivation. During the same period, Government of India released Rs. 1,447.21 crore to the implementing States under various components of the Mission.
The NMEO-OP was approved for the period 2021-22 to 2025-26 with an outlay of Rs. 11,040 crores. Subsequently, Annual Action Plans (AAPs) of 2026-27 for implementing states have been approved for Rs. 1143.9 crore.
In addition to NMEO-OP, the National Mission on Edible Oils – Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) was launched on 3rd October, 2024 for seven years period from 2024-25 to 2030-31 to boost the domestic oilseed production and to strive toward self-sufficiency in edible oil. Under the mission, production of improved indigenous varieties and hybrids of oilseeds are being promoted through 100% support for purchase of breeder seeds and also promoted through distribution of certified seeds in the Value Chain Clusters. 60 Seed Hubs & 50 specialized seed storage units have been sanctioned for production of Breeder Seed of recently released varieties.

title: STEPS TO INCREASE PRODUCTION OF OILSEEDS AND PULSES
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Mission on Edible Oils-Oilseeds (NMEO-OS) was approved on 3rd October, 2024 to boost domestic oilseed production and to strive towards self-reliance in edible oils. The mission aims to increase primary oilseed production from 39 million tonnes (2022-23) to 69.7 million tonnes by 2030-31.
The Government has launched the Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses on 11th October, 2025 to increase the domestic production of pulses. The mission aims to increase pulse production from 242 lakh tonnes to 350 lakh tonnes by 2030-31.
The NMEO-OS is implemented through a cluster-based approach with market linkages. Over 600 Value Chain Clusters have been operationalized across the country which are managed by Value Chain Partners such as Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), cooperatives and other agencies. Under these clusters, farmers are provided free high-quality seeds of latest high yielding varieties and training on good agricultural practices. T
he mission supports the establishment and upgradation of post-harvest infrastructure (oil mills) to improve oil recovery from primary and secondary sources.
The mission focuses on improving the productivity through Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs), Cluster Frontline Demonstrations (CFLDs) and Block-Level Demonstrations (BLDs) to help farmers to adopt latest high yielding varieties and good agricultural practices. The mission strengthens availability of certified seeds through 100% support for purchase of breeder seeds, establishment of new seed hubs and specialised seed storage units in the public sector to enhance production and storage capacity.
Procurement of oilseeds from farmers also ensured at Minimum Support Price (MSP) through Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA).
Under the mission, 13.52 lakh hectares were covered under free seed distribution in Value Chain Clusters during 2025-26 and 4.44 lakh hectare area covered so far during kharif, 2026. 60 Seed Hubs & 50 specialized seed storage units have been sanctioned for production of Breeder Seeds of recently released varieties. Oilseeds production has increased from 413. 55 lakh tonnes in 2022-23 to 430.59 lakh tonnes in 2025-26 (3rd Advance Estimate, DA&FW).
As reported by the Directorate of Sugar and Vegetable Oils, Department of Food and Public Distribution, the domestic availability of edible oils increased from 124.23 lakh tonnes in 2022–23 to 126.30 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 and edible oil imports declined from 165.00 lakh tonnes in 2022–23 to 160.72 lakh tonnes in 2024–25.
Under the Pulses Mission, assistance is provided to pulses farmers through State Governments/UTs on various interventions such as seed production, distribution of certified seeds of high yielding & climate resilient varieties and demonstration of latest crop production technologies, capacity building, seed kit distribution and strengthening post-harvest infrastructure. To ensure remunerative prices to farmers, the Mission supports assured procurement of Tur, Urad, Masoor from registered and willing farmers by National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India Ltd. (NAFED) and National Cooperative Consumers' Federation of India Limited (NCCF) under Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) based on requisitions made by the States.
During 2025-26, under the mission 4.79 lakh ha demonstrations were conducted on latest crop production & protection technologies, 4.33 lakh qtls of quality seeds were produced, 3.10 lakh qtls of certified seeds were distributed and 9.25 lakh seedkits were distributed free of cost to the farmers. The production of pulses has increased from 242.46 lakh tonnes during 2023-24 to 274.09 lakh tonnes during 2025-26 (3rd Advance estimate). Pulse imports declined from 72.56 lakh tonnes in 2024–25 to 59.64 lakh tonnes in 2025–26, reflecting improved domestic availability.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR
in a written reply in Rajya  Sabha today.

date:

                07 AUG 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) is implementing National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (NBHM) a Central Sector Scheme through National Bee Board (NBB).
The objectives of National Beekeeping and Honey Mission are to promote scientific beekeeping for holistic growth of beekeeping industry, increasing production of honey and beehive products,  income & employment generation, providing livelihood support to farm and non-farm households, women empowerment through beekeeping, to strengthen beekeepers by developing institutional framework through collective approach and to enhance agriculture/ horticulture production. Under the scheme project based assistance is provided to eligible Implementing Agencies (IAs) forwarded by the Central/ State Nodal Agencies for various activities. These include setting up of Integrated Beekeeping Development Centers, honey testing labs, bee disease diagnostic labs, Quality Nucleus Stock Development Centre, capacity building, technology demonstration, empowerment of women through beekeeping etc. NBHM also supports marketing, branding, value addition and Research & Development.
National Beekeeping and Honey Mission supplements the efforts of State Governments; Implementing Agencies and Stakeholder organizations to increase honey production, scientific beekeeping and enhancing agricultural productivity through project based approach, as per provisions of NBHM.
So far 7 world class honey testing labs, 66 mini labs to check adulteration, 83 honey processing units and 90 collection, branding & packaging units have been established. These support efficient storage and marketing. 81 Quality Nucleus Stock Development Centres  have been supported for producing quality queen bees and colony multiplication so far. Production of Honey increased from 80,530 MT in 2014–15 to 1,51,690 MT as per Horticulture Crops Statistics (2nd Advance Estimates 2025-26) in 2025-26.

title: SECL leads India in Scientific Mine Closure, Transforming abandoned Mines into Sustainable Community Assets
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) has emerged as India's leader in scientific mine closure, having successfully completed the scientific closure of 28 abandoned mines, the highest among Coal India subsidiaries. The company accounts for 67 per cent of all abandoned mines scientifically closed in the country, while 25 mines were scientifically closed during FY 2025-26, the highest achieved by any organisation in India in a single year.
At SECL, mine closure is regarded as an integral stage of the mining lifecycle rather than the conclusion of mining activity. Once coal extraction is complete, the focus shifts to securing the site, restoring the landscape and preparing the land for productive future use through scientific reclamation and repurposing.
Of the 54 abandoned mines identified for scientific closure, SECL completed the closure of three mines during FY 2024-25 and 25 mines during FY 2025-26. The company has set targets to close 11 mines in FY 2026-27 and the remaining 15 mines in FY 2027-28, completing the scientific closure of all identified abandoned mines in phases.
To strengthen planning and stakeholder participation, District Mine Closure Advisory Committees (DMCACs) have been constituted across all 10 operational districts in Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh.
Scientific mine closure at SECL involves securing abandoned mine workings through permanent sealing of underground openings, demolition of redundant infrastructure, treatment of subsidence areas, installation of safety measures, land reclamation, plantation and ecological restoration. Reclaimed land is subsequently assessed for productive reuse to support renewable energy, community infrastructure, livelihoods and environmental conservation. The company is currently implementing eight mine repurposing projects.
Among its major initiatives, the Kenapara Eco Park at Bishrampur has already been completed on reclaimed mine land. At Vivek Nagar UG, a 5 MW solar power project integrated with an Eco Park is under implementation. SECL has also commissioned 20 MW solar power plants at Bhatgaon and Bishrampur, while a 40 MW solar project at Pinoura UG is under implementation. In addition, a 55 MW solar power project at Jamuna UG and Govinda UG has been planned, extending the productive use of reclaimed mine land for renewable energy generation.
Several scientifically closed mines have also been repurposed into public infrastructure. At Korba 3&4 UG, reclaimed mine land has been integrated into the Bal Vihar Higher Secondary School campus. North Jhagrakhand UG now supports a public park and a water filter plant, while a former service building at Subhash Incline has been repurposed into a municipal water filter plant. At South Jhagrakhand 5&6 UG, a former mine service building has been converted into a CISF Post, while South Jhagrakhand 10&11 UG has been developed into a public park. Banki 7&8 UG now houses a health centre and a weekly market, while Banki 5&6 UG has been developed as a community centre.
Environmental restoration remains central to every mine closure project. At Chachai UG, nearly 35,000 saplings have been planted following the sealing of mine openings and demolition of obsolete structures. Dense plantations have also been developed at sites including Ramnagar UG, Korea UG and Malga UG, while naturally regenerated vegetation has been preserved at Rajgamar 8&9 UG and Pure Chirimiri UG to support ecological recovery.
Alongside environmental restoration, SECL has organised skill development programmes and health camps across reclaimed mine areas. Training has covered computer education, tailoring, handicrafts, mushroom cultivation, pickle making and other livelihood activities for project-affected communities.
The company is also promoting sustainable livelihoods through productive utilisation of reclaimed mine land and mine water bodies. Pisciculture initiatives are expected to support annual fish production of 25 tonnes, generate 206 livelihoods and provide a potential annual income of ₹3 lakh per participating family.
Future repurposing proposals include eco-tourism, pisciculture, poultry farming and masala processing at Jamuna OC; honey processing, turmeric cultivation and cage culture at Baiga OC; and a training centre, compressed bio-gas (CBG) plant and fruit-bearing plantations at Banki UG, based on local conditions and future land-use requirements.
SECL Chairman-cum-Managing Director Harish Duhan said scientific mine closure represents the responsible completion of the mining lifecycle and reflects the company's commitment to sustainable mining.
"At SECL, mine closure is not the end of mining but the beginning of a new chapter. Our objective is to restore land, protect the environment and convert reclaimed mine areas into productive assets that generate clean energy, support livelihoods and serve local communities. Every scientifically closed mine reflects our commitment to responsible mining and sustainable development," Duhan said.

title: India successfully concludes the 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting in Jaipur under its BRICS Chairship 2026.
subtitle:
The Chair’s Statement and Outcome Document was issued comprising four Annexes.

BRICS Members commended India’s leadership for progress towards finalising the Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership 2030.

Government safeguards the interests of India's farmers, securing food and livelihood security and to preserve Special and Differential Treatment for developing countries in the Multilateral Trading System, with the World Trade Organization at its core

Jaipur Consensus and Guiding Principles for MSME credit agreed to close the trade finance gap and expand small businesses' access to global markets

India champions balanced and expanding trade among BRICS, greater trade in services and resilient & diversified Global Value Chains
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 8:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting concluded successfully today at Jaipur, Rajasthan, under India's BRICS Chairship, 2026. The Meeting was chaired by Shri Piyush Goyal, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry and was attended by Shri Jitin Prasada, Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry and Shri Rajesh Agrawal, Commerce Secretary. Held under the overarching theme,
"Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability"
, the meeting was preceded by the Third Meeting of the BRICS
Contact Group on Economic and Trade Issues (CGETI)
, held on 3 and 4 August 2026 in New Delhi.
The Meeting brought together Trade Ministers, Vice Ministers, Heads of Delegation and officials from the BRICS member countries. The visiting dignitaries included H.E. Mr. Marcio Fernando Elias Rosa, Minister of State for Development, Industry, Commerce and Services of Brazil; H.E. Mr. Li Chenggang, China International Trade Representative and Vice Minister of Commerce of China; H.E. Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt; H.E. Mr. Molalign Asfaw Ayana, Ambassador of Ethiopia; H.E. Dr. Budi Santoso, Minister of Trade of Indonesia; H.E. Dr. Mohammad Sadegh Mofatteh, First Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry of Iran; H.E. Mr. Vladimir Evgenievich Ilichev, Deputy Minister of Economic Development of Russia; H.E. Mr. Parks Franklyn Mpho Tau, Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition of South Africa; and H.E. Dr. Thani bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi, Minister of Foreign Trade of the United Arab Emirates.
Earlier in the day, the visiting Ministers and delegates undertook a walkthrough of the historic City Palace at Jaipur and appreciated India's rich heritage and vibrant craft traditions of Rajasthan.
The Ministerial meeting started with opening remarks by the Commerce Secretary, followed by the welcome address of the Minister of State for Commerce and Industry and keynote address of the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry. Guided by Hon’ble Prime Minister of India Shri Narendra Modi’s vision, the Commerce and Industry Minister unequivocally pushed for safeguarding the interests of India's farmers, securing food and livelihood security. He further stated that BRICS countries account for a rising share in the world economy and the Group stood for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. He reaffirmed India's vision of a reformed, development-oriented, member-driven and consensus-based multilateral trading system, with the World Trade Organization at its core, preserving Special and Differential Treatment for developing countries and restoration of a fully functioning, two-tier and binding dispute settlement system. The Minister underlined that the most-favoured-nation principle, together with Special and Differential Treatment, remains the cornerstone of a fair, inclusive, non-discriminatory and rules-based order and that reform must strengthen this cornerstone, not dilute it. He set out India's priorities for the Chairship: strengthening the multilateral trading system; building resilient and diversified global value chains; internationalisation of MSMEs and their access to trade finance; and seamless flow of digitally delivered services across borders.
Delivering the Welcome Address, the Minister of State for Commerce and Industry welcomed the Ministers and delegates to Jaipur in the spirit of Padharo Mhare Desh, and recalled that BRICS cooperation, guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of Humanity First, places people at its centre. He affirmed that the true promise of intra-BRICS trade is focused on human welfare, lies in the fortunes of micro, small and medium enterprises, in women-led businesses and in the energy of the youth of developing economies.
Trade Ministers of the member countries shared their national perspectives and emphasized the greater role of BRICS in furthering global trade. The Meeting concluded with a summary by the Commerce Secretary on behalf of the Indian Chairship and the Concluding Remarks of the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, with the Trade Ministers thanking India for its hospitality and its leadership of BRICS 2026.
The Annex-I affirms the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, with development at its centre, the preservation of Special and Differential Treatment, and the restoration of a fully functioning, two-tier and binding dispute settlement system, alongside the policy space for developing economies for their food and livelihood security.
The Meeting gave a decisive push for small business entrepreneurs. Ministers issued the Jaipur Consensus to study a BRICS Invoice Discounting Mechanism and adopted the Guiding Principles for Credit Assessment Frameworks for Export-Oriented MSMEs, so that a firm is judged by its cash flow and not by its assets and collateral. These instruments respond directly to the global trade finance gap of about USD 2.5 trillion which impacts smaller enterprises and therefore form part of the Workplan on the Internationalisation of MSMEs adopted as Annex-II.
Ministers also advanced the opening of markets and economic diversification among BRICS Members. The Workplan on the BRICS Shared Understanding on Global Value Chains, covered by Annex-III, carries the GVC Action Plan 2026-2030, including BRICS Technical Council, BRICS Connect, BRICS GVC Joint Study, the possibility of establishing strategic supply chain and investment promotion platform including in pharmaceutical sector as well as food security, among others.
The BRICS Principles to Facilitate Digitally Delivered Services Across Borders, adopted as the Annex-IV will help cooperation in safe and secure digitally delivered services. Together with the pursuit of balanced and expanding trade among members, these outcomes place services and value chains at the frontier of the next decade of BRICS cooperation.
Another outcome was the progress towards finalisation of the Strategy for BRICS Economic Partnership 2030, spanning the Multilateral Trading System, trade in services, the digital economy, industry, innovation and technology, trade and investment, financial cooperation and sustainable development. Ministers agreed to submit the Strategy, together with the priorities to the BRICS Leaders for endorsement.
The 16th BRICS Trade Ministers' Meeting marks a significant milestone under India's BRICS Chairship and reaffirms India's commitment to an open, inclusive, transparent, equitable and rules-based multilateral trading system with the WTO at its core. The outcomes of the Meeting, anchored in the interests of farmers and small enterprises, would contribute to India's vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 and to a future of shared prosperity among emerging economies.

title: DGFT Connects DPIIT-Recognised Startups to Global Trade Ecosystem via ‘Source from India’ Feature
subtitle: Start-Ups To Receive Dedicated "Start-Up Badge" On Official Buyer Discovery Platform
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 6:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a major step towards promoting innovation-led exports and strengthening India's global trade ecosystem, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Department of Commerce, has expanded the eligibility criteria for the "Source from India" service on the Trade Connect ePlatform to include eligible DPIIT-recognised Start-ups.
The decision, notified through a Trade Notice no. 16 dated August 06, 2026 issued today, aims to provide greater international visibility to India's growing start-up ecosystem by enabling innovative exporters to showcase their products and capabilities on the Government's official digital buyer discovery platform.
Trade Connect, launched by the Department of Commerce, serves as a one-stop digital interface connecting Indian exporters with trade-related services and institutional support. One of its flagship features, "Source from India," enables eligible exporters to create dedicated digital microsites that allow international buyers to discover reliable Indian suppliers and connect with them directly.
Under the revised framework, with effect from August 06, 2026, DPIIT-recognised Start-ups meeting the existing eligibility criteria under "Source from India" will be able to create their microsites on the platform and will be identified through a unique Start-up Badge, making them easily discoverable by overseas buyers.
Further, to encourage early-stage exporters, a special onboarding provision has also been introduced. DPIIT-recognised Start-ups possessing an active Import Export Code (IEC) that is not in the Denied Entity List (DEL) will also be eligible to create their profiles on "Source from India", even if they do not presently fulfil the standard export performance criteria. Their onboarding will be subject to verification through the DGFT IEC database.
The initiative is expected to significantly strengthen the participation of innovation-driven enterprises in international trade by providing them with enhanced visibility on an official Government platform. It is also expected to support export diversification, promote technology-led products and services, and reinforce India's emergence as a global hub for innovation and entrepreneurship.
Start-up users already registered on Trade Connect whose accounts are linked to eligible IECs will automatically receive the option to create their "Source from India" microsites from their dashboard. A detailed user guide has also been issued to facilitate seamless registration and profile creation.
The revised framework builds upon the earlier expansion of "Source from India", under which all valid IEC holders meeting the prescribed export realisation criteria became eligible to join the platform. By extending the initiative to India's start-up ecosystem, the Government seeks to create new opportunities for innovative enterprises to access global markets while further strengthening India's export competitiveness.
About Trade Connect ePlatform
Trade Connect is the Government of India's integrated digital platform designed to provide exporters with access to trade-related information, services, market intelligence and institutional support through a single interface. Its flagship "Source from India" feature serves as an official digital marketplace where international buyers can identify verified Indian exporters, view their product offerings and business credentials, and establish direct business connections.

The Protocol of the 12th Session of the Working Group was signed by both the co-chairs reaffirming the strategic India-Russia partnership with the aim to deepen industrial and economic cooperation. The session was attended by around 60 delegates from both sides.

title: GeM Completes a Decade of Transforming Public Procurement with Cumulative GMV Exceeding ₹20 Lakh Crore
subtitle: IIT Delhi Study Estimates ₹1.76 Lakh Crore in Net Social Savings through GeM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 5:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government e Marketplace (GeM) will complete ten years of operations on 9 August 2026. Marking a decade of transforming public procurement through technology, transparency, efficiency and good governance, the platform has facilitated a cumulative Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) of over ₹20 lakh crore through more than 3.78 crore orders, underscoring its growing role in India’s public procurement ecosystem.
The platform’s annual GMV has grown from ₹422 crore in FY 2016–17 to over ₹5 lakh crore in each of FY 2024–25 and FY 2025–26. In the first four months of FY 2026–27 alone, GeM recorded a GMV of ₹1,47,888 crore. While the platform took more than eight years to achieve its first ₹10 lakh crore in cumulative GMV, the next ₹10 lakh crore milestone was reached in less than two years, reflecting accelerated adoption and increasing participation across the public procurement ecosystem.
Participation on the platform has expanded significantly over the past decade. The number of profile-completed sellers has increased from 3,339 to 25.45 lakh, while primary buyer organisations have grown from 1,707 to 1.37 lakh. The number of Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) registered on the platform has increased from 2,424 to 12.25 lakh.
GeM has also played a significant role in promoting inclusive public procurement. MSEs have fulfilled orders worth more than ₹9.07 lakh crore, accounting for 45.6 per cent of the cumulative GMV. More than 2.24 lakh women-led MSEs have fulfilled over 50 lakh orders valued at more than ₹99,147 crore, while 42,242 startups have secured orders worth over ₹65,633 crore through the platform.
An IIT Delhi study covering FY 2023–24 to FY 2025–26 estimated a monetised benefit of ₹86,571.69 crore through price and process efficiencies, resulting in a net social saving of ₹1,76,411.46 crore. The study also found that, in a comparison of 101 items with other e-marketplaces, GeM offered lower prices for 74.3 per cent of the items, with a spend-weighted saving of 13.6 per cent. Earlier assessments in the Economic Survey 2021–22 had also recorded consistent procurement savings through the platform.
To further improve ease of doing business, GeM has introduced several seller-friendly measures. Transaction charges have been reduced from 0.50 per cent to 0.30 per cent, while orders up to ₹10 lakh have been exempted from transaction charges. As a result, 97 per cent of all orders now attract no transaction fee. The maximum transaction fee has been capped at ₹3 lakh, and vendor assessment fees have been reduced by up to 92 per cent.
According to the interim findings of an Axis My India survey, 92 per cent of the buyers surveyed expressed satisfaction with their overall experience on the platform. Among sellers, 67 per cent reported higher business volumes, while 78 per cent indicated their intention to continue using the platform.
GeM now digitises the entire public procurement lifecycle and deploys Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) tools to identify suspected cartelisation, collusion and order splitting. As a fully digital platform, it also generates a rich transactional data trail that enables policymakers to monitor public procurement spending, identify inefficiencies and design evidence-based policy interventions.
Chief Executive Officer, GeM, Shri Mihir Kumar, said, “GeM has moved public procurement from opaque, fragmented processes to a single, transparent marketplace where capability determines success. The next decade will be defined by deeper use of AI for better value for the public and equal opportunity for every enterprise.”
Building on a decade of transformation, GeM will continue to strengthen the use of data-driven technologies to promote fair competition, enhance value for public expenditure and build a procurement ecosystem that is simpler, faster, more transparent and value-driven for buyers and sellers alike, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat.

title: Union Minister of Home Affairs and Cooperation Shri Amit Shah to inaugurate NUCFDC's new office in Mumbai tomorrow
subtitle:
Security Operations Centre and nationwide Core Banking Service for Urban Cooperative Banks to be launched at the ‘Sahakar Nav-Kranti’ programme

Memorandum of Understanding between NUCFDC and National Forensic Sciences University to also be exchanged

Significant initiative to make the Urban Cooperative Banking sector modern, secure and competitive in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 7:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Taking forward Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of ‘Sahkar Se Samriddhi’, Union Minister of Home Affairs and Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will inaugurate the new office of the National Urban Co-operative Finance and Development Corporation Limited—NUCFDC at Sharda Sadan, Fort, Mumbai, on 8 August 2026. On the occasion, Shri Amit Shah will also interact with representatives of State Urban Cooperative Bank Federations and district associations of Maharashtra.
Thereafter, Union Minister of Home Affairs and Cooperation Shri Amit Shah will participate as the Chief Guest in the ‘Sahakar Nav-Kranti’ programme at the BSE International Convention Centre. Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis will also be present at the programme.
During the programme, a Memorandum of Understanding will be exchanged between NUCFDC and the National Forensic Sciences University—NFSU. This collaboration will play an important role in strengthening cyber security, technological capabilities and institutional capacity in the Urban Cooperative Banking sector.
The Union Minister of Home Affairs and Cooperation will also inaugurate a Security Operations Centre—SOC to strengthen the cyber security of Urban Cooperative Banks. A Core Banking Service and allied services under a nationwide service bundle will also be launched. These initiatives aim to provide Urban Cooperative Banks with a modern, secure and shared digital banking infrastructure. Representatives of the first six Urban Cooperative Banks successfully connected to ‘Sahakar CBS’ will also be felicitated during the programme.
On the occasion, the Union Minister of Home Affairs and Cooperation will also release the book titled ‘Operational Risk Management – A Practical Guide to Urban Co-operative Banks’, authored by Shri G. P. Mistry, former Deputy General Manager of the Reserve Bank of India. The book provides practical guidance to Urban Cooperative Banks on the identification, assessment and effective management of operational risks.
NUCFDC was launched on 2 March 2024 as an umbrella organisation for Urban Cooperative Banks. It aims to provide these banks with shared technology platforms, core banking services, cyber-security solutions, capacity-building and operational support. Through shared services, particularly small and medium Urban Cooperative Banks will be able to reduce the cost of adopting modern banking technology, offer improved services to customers and compete effectively with private and commercial banks.

title: IEPFA Organises Stakeholder Engagement with Nodal Officers of Companies on Integrated IEPFA Portal 2.0
subtitle: Engagement session focuses on enhancing digital claim processing, stakeholder collaboration, and user-centric reforms
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 6:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority (IEPFA), under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India, in collaboration with the National e-Governance Division (NeGD), organised a
Stakeholder Engagement Session
with Companies’ Nodal Officers on the Integrated IEPFA Portal 2.0. The session served as an interactive platform to demonstrate the proposed Claimant and e-Verification Report (EVR) modules of the new portal and to obtain valuable feedback from Companies’ Nodal Officers ahead of its rollout.
The session was led by
Ms. Anita Shah Akella, CEO, IEPFA and Joint Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs
, along with senior officials of IEPFA, the NeGD project team, and Companies’ Nodal Officers. Participants were provided with a detailed walkthrough of the modernised portal, which introduces several digital-first features aimed at simplifying the investor claim process and improving operational efficiency.
Key features presented during the session included digital KYC integration, pre-filled Form IEPF-5, an entitlement search facility, a simplified three-step workflow for filing e-Verification Reports (EVRs), and provisions relating to Rule 7(3) for additional (delay) fees. The implementation roadmap was also shared with stakeholders, outlining User Acceptance Testing (UAT) in August 2026, stakeholder training in September, pilot implementation in October, and the planned launch of the Integrated IEPFA Portal 2.0 in November 2026.
Companies’ Nodal Officers actively participated in the discussions and shared practical suggestions based on their operational experience. Recommendations included Aadhaar eKYC address validation with companies records, mandatory KYC verification of Authorised Representatives, a comprehensive validation checklist before issuance of Entitlement Letters, bulk DSC and eSign capabilities, integration of approved IEPF Form-4 data into the EVR module, share valuation based on NSE and BSE data with application of the lower value, and automated alerts to identify frequent address changes as a fraud prevention measure.
The suggestions and recommendations received during the session have been shared with the NeGD team for consideration while finalising the portal. The stakeholder engagement forms part of IEPFA's ongoing efforts to develop the Integrated IEPFA Portal 2.0 through continuous engagement with Companies’ Nodal Officers and other stakeholders. The Authority remains committed to leveraging technology to simplify claim settlement, strengthen transparency, improve service delivery, and build a secure, efficient, and investor-centric digital ecosystem.
IEPFA
under Ministry of Corporate Affairs
is dedicated to promoting investor awareness and protection through sustained outreach, investor education, and strategic collaborations. The Authority continues to introduce technology-enabled reforms and citizen-centric initiatives to facilitate efficient claim settlement and strengthen investor services across the country.

title: Union Minister for Education Reaffirms India's Commitment to a People-Centric and Humanity-First Approach to BRICS Cooperation, at the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting
subtitle:
Innovation is Essential to Ensure Education Systems Continuously Evolve to Meet the Aspirations of Future Generations, Says Shri Pralhad Joshi

Meeting Concludes in Bhubaneswar with the Adoption of the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Declaration
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Education Shri Pralhad Joshi today reaffirmed
India's commitment to a people-centric and humanity-first approach to BRICS cooperation.
He was chairing the
13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Meeting which concluded in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, with the adoption of the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Declaration.
Reiterating India's commitment to working closely with all the BRICS partners, the Union Minister expressed confidence that the momentum generated during the Meeting would translate into meaningful action. Referring to India's BRICS Chairship 2026, theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," the Minister said that education systems must prepare young people for emerging opportunities while remaining firmly rooted in human values.
He added that learners, teachers, researchers and young people should remain at the centre of policymaking and international cooperation.
Shri Joshi remarked that education was the foundation of inclusive growth and shared prosperity, and that the adopted Declaration reflected the collective commitment of BRICS nations to strengthen cooperation across the five priority areas. He also
stressed on the importance of preserving and promoting traditional and indigenous knowledge systems, observing that innovation and heritage complement one another. He noted that the rich civilisational traditions of BRICS nations presented a unique opportunity to preserve traditional knowledge, study it rigorously, and pass on its value to future generations.
The Minister also highlighted Odisha's rich legacy as an ancient centre of learning and reflected on India's enduring civilizational values of "Atithi Devo Bhava" and "Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam". He emphasised that while nations may differ in their traditions and experiences, their progress was interconnected.
Ministers, senior officials and delegates from BRICS member countries, including Brazil, Russia, China, South Africa, Indonesia, Iran, Ethiopia and United Arab Emirates attended the Meeting aimed at advancing cooperation under the BRICS Education Track.
The adoption of the 13th BRICS Education Ministers’ Declaration reaffirmed education as a key pillar of BRICS cooperation and outlined a shared roadmap across five priority areas identified under India's Chairship. The outcomes are as following:
Strengthening Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) and Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN):
It was agreed to promote universal and inclusive access to quality ECCE, strengthen school readiness, and encourage the use of age-appropriate digital solutions for early learning.
Strengthening Cooperation in Skill Development and TVET:
The role of the BRICS TVET Cooperation Alliance (BRICS-TCA) in advancing collaboration was recognised, including through the forthcoming Biennial Progress Report and Compendium of Sustainable Skill Initiatives. The Declaration also acknowledged India's initiative to undertake an International Skill Gap Study, with participation by interested BRICS members on a voluntary basis.
Enhancing Research, Innovation and Start-up Ecosystems:
It was agreed to promote joint research, encourage the safe, ethical and human-centred use of Artificial Intelligence in education, strengthen innovation-driven entrepreneurship, and deepen collaboration among higher education institutions, researchers and start-up ecosystems.
Advancing Mutual Recognition of Qualifications (MRQ):
It was agreed to convene meetings of the Working Group to carry forward deliberations on a Memorandum of Understanding on Mutual Recognition of Qualifications, with a view to facilitating greater academic mobility and cooperation.
Strengthening Capacity Building for Academic Leadership and Institutional Development:
Continued organisation of the BRICS Rectors' Forum, faculty and leadership exchanges, scholarship programmes with a focus on STEM, and exploratory work towards a BRICS University Global Ranking and Evaluation System were encouraged.
The Meeting also welcomed India's initiative on the BRICS Guiding Principles on Strengthening Academic Collaboration on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems and suggested that the BRICS Network University may consider the inclusion of traditional and indigenous knowledge systems as an additional International Thematic Group.
The Ministry of Education also hosted the 3rd BRICS Senior Officials’ Meeting (SOM) under India’s BRICS chairship 2026, on August 5, 2026 in Bhubaneswar. The discussions reaffirmed the shared commitment of member countries towards advancing inclusive, resilient and future-ready education systems through greater cooperation, innovation and knowledge exchange.
India will continue to host BRICS Ministerial Meetings across various sectors during its Chairship, culminating in the
18th BRICS Summit
, scheduled to be held in
New Delhi on September 12–13, 2026
.

title: Union Environment Minister graces Haryana’s 77th Van Mahotsav celebrations at Manesar; plants a sapling on the occasion
subtitle:
Van Mahotsav not merely a programme but opportunity to repay our debt to Nature: Haryana CM Shri Nayab Singh Saini

Shri Bhupender Yadav congratulates Haryana for actively working on Centre’s recommendations to protect Aravallis and prevent Air Pollution
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 2:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today graced Haryana’s 77th Van Mahotsav, organised at Manesar. Dignitaries present on the dais included CM (Haryana), Shri Nayab Singh Saini, State Minister for Environment and Forests, Shri Rao Narbir Singh, public representatives and senior officials of the State Government.
Addressing the event, Shri Yadav congratulated the State Government for its efforts to make Gurugram not just a millennium city but also a green city. He highlighted that Haryana is actively working on Centre’s recommendations to protect Aravallis and prevent Air Pollution. The Minister also congratulated sportspersons, especially girls from Haryana, for bringing laurels to the country in the recently concluded Commonwealth Games.
Shri Yadav informed that he had reviewed the air quality situation in Haryana a few days ago and was happy to note that the State Government has taken cognisance of his recommendations and worked to carry them forward. The recommendations, inter alia, included housing societies to have solid waste management rules in place, industries to install Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs), implementation of smart traffic management and greening activities be undertaken. Shri Yadav stressed the importance of grasslands and woodlands for soil conservation and maintaining the water table, and added that good work has been done in the state in this regard.
Addressing the gathering, Haryana Chief Minister Shri Nayab Singh Saini said that Van Mahotsav is not merely a programme for planting saplings but an opportunity to repay our debt to nature. He said that while the world today talks of environmental protection, India accorded nature the status of worship thousands of years ago.
Shri Saini said the Prime Minister has given the guiding mantra of planting ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’, under which a target of 1.4 crore trees has been set for the State this year, with the participation of different stakeholders ensured. He said it is the collective responsibility of all to make the Aravallis green again.
The Chief Minister informed that the major highlight of this year's celebrations was that District-Level Van Mahotsav programmes were simultaneously organized across all the districts of Haryana. The events were graced by State Ministers, Members of Parliament, Members of the Legislative Assembly, Chairpersons of Boards and Corporations, Deputy Commissioners and other public representatives of the respective districts, he added.
Earlier during the event, the dignitaries planted saplings, administered the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ pledge, and released two publications – ‘Haryana Forest News’ and ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’. Winners of the quiz, painting and other competitions, held on the theme of ‘Swachh Haryana, Harit Haryana’, were awarded.

title: DRI intensifies vigil along India's North-Eastern Frontier
subtitle: DRI seizes 15 kg Methamphetamine; 11 MT foreign-origin poppy seeds; and 10 MT areca nuts smuggled from Myanmar in three major operations; three persons arrested
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 3:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Continuing its sustained crackdown on cross-border smuggling and narcotics trafficking along India's North-Eastern frontier, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) carried out a series of intelligence-driven operations in Mizoram and Assam, resulting in the seizure of 15 kg Methamphetamine tablets, around 11 MT of foreign-origin poppy seeds, and 10 MT of smuggled foreign-origin areca nuts.
In a major intelligence led narcotics interdiction yesterday, officers of DRI intercepted an ambulance near Sakei Bangla, about 40 km from Aizawl on the Aizawl–Champhai Road, suspected to be transporting narcotic drugs under the guise of a medical emergency. Examination of the ambulance revealed 15 brick-shaped packets containing 15 kg pinkish-orange Methamphetamine tablets, a psychotropic substances, concealed inside a white HDPE bag placed beside a patient bed on which a dummy patient was lying. Preliminary investigation revealed that the contraband had been smuggled into Mizoram from Myanmar through the Champhai–Zokhawthar sector and was destined for further transportation to Assam. The recovered Methamphetamine along with ambulance used to transport have been seized under the NDPS Act, 1985. The ambulance driver and two accomplices have been arrested.
Methamphetamine tablets, commonly known as “Yaba”, is a highly addictive synthetic stimulant that affects the central nervous system. Illicitly manufactured methamphetamine tablets are trafficked from Myanmar and are known to cause severe physical and psychological harm, including addiction, aggression, paranoia and long-term neurological damage. Owing to its high abuse potential, methamphetamine, a psychotropic substance is regulated under the NDPS Act, 1985, and remains a major focus area for narcotics enforcement agencies worldwide.
During the intervening night of 5th and 6th August 2026, in another intelligence-led operation, officers of DRI, assisted by Assam Rifles conducted searches at a godown in Badarpur, Karimganj district, Assam. The operation resulted in the recovery of around 11 MTs foreign-origin poppy seeds concealed inside HDPE bags bearing markings of commercial tea consignments, carton packages and loose stock scattered across the premises. Preliminary investigation indicated that the goods had been smuggled into India through the porous Indo-Myanmar border for onward distribution to various parts of the country. The poppy seeds, valued at approximately Rs.1.67 crore, has been seized under the Customs Act, 1962.
Poppy seeds are widely used as a food ingredient and spice in several cuisines; however, their import into India is subject to stringent regulatory controls. Under India's Foreign Trade Policy, poppy seeds can be imported only from designated countries and through a registration mechanism administered by the Central Bureau of Narcotics. These safeguards are intended to ensure traceability and prevent misuse of illicitly cultivated produce entering legitimate supply chains. Smuggling of unregulated foreign-origin poppy seeds not only circumvents these controls but also adversely impacts lawful trade and regulatory oversight.
Earlier, on 05.08.2026, officers of DRI intercepted a consignment from a Train No. 22411 at Rangia Railway Station and recovered 120 bags containing 10 MT of foreign-origin areca nuts from the parcel van of the train. Preliminary investigation revealed that the consignment had been smuggled into India from Myanmar and was being transported to markets outside the North-East region. The seized areca nuts, valued at approximately Rs 1 crore, have been seized under the Customs Act, 1962.
Areca nut, commonly known as supari, is one of the most frequently smuggled commodities across India's North-Eastern borders. Large-scale smuggling of foreign-origin areca nuts causes significant loss of government revenue and adversely affects the livelihoods of domestic growers. The illicit trade in areca nuts has emerged as a recurring enforcement concern due to its links with organised smuggling networks operating in border areas.

title: Steps taken to Reduce Out-of-Pocket Expenditure on Healthcare by Households
subtitle:
AB PM-JAY provides ₹5 lakh annual health cover to over 12 crore vulnerable families

Ayushman Vay Vandana provides health coverage to 6 crore senior citizens aged 70 years and above irrespective of socio-economic status

1.87 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs operationalized across the country to deliver comprehensive primary healthcare services

Free Drugs and Free Diagnostics Initiatives rolled out nationwide to reduce Out-of-Pocket Expenditure on healthcare

Government strengthens affordable healthcare ecosystem through NHM, AB PM-JAY, PM-ABHIM and PMSSY
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                07 AUG 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government has undertaken a range of measures to reduce Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) on healthcare by expanding access to free and affordable health services, strengthening healthcare infrastructure, and providing financial protection to households across the country.
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) supplements the efforts of the States and Union Territories (UTs) in expanding affordable healthcare services and strengthening healthcare infrastructure across the country, through various Centrally Sponsored Schemes and Central Sector Schemes. Towards this end, MoHFW is implementing schemes such as National Health Mission (NHM), Ayushman Bharat- Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), Pradhan Mantri- Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM), Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY).
Under the NHM, the Government has taken many steps towards universal health coverage by supporting the State Governments in providing accessible and affordable healthcare to people. 1.87 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandir (AAM) have been operationalized across the country to deliver the expanded range of comprehensive primary healthcare services that include preventive, promotive, curative, palliative and rehabilitative services. These include reproductive and child healthcare services, communicable and non-communicable diseases, and a wide array of other health concerns.
National Free Drugs Service Initiative and Free Diagnostics Service Initiative have been rolled out to ensure availability of essential drugs and diagnostic facilities, and reduce Out- of-Pocket Expenditure of the patients visiting public health facilities. This includes financial support to States/UTs for 113 drugs at AAM-Sub Health Centres, 179 at AAM-Primary Health Centres, 301 at Community Health Centres, 318 at Sub- District Hospitals and 381 at District Hospitals. Besides, quality generic medicines are made available at affordable prices to all, under Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) in collaboration with the State Governments. Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment (AMRIT) Pharmacy stores have been set up in some hospitals/institutions.
In addition, Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) provides health cover of ₹5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization to more than 12 crore families constituting the economically vulnerable bottom 40% of India’s population. States/UTs implementing AB PM-JAY have further expanded the beneficiary base, at their own cost. Further, the scheme has been expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age 70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio- economic status under AB PM-JAY with Vay Vandana Card.
The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare,
Smt. Anupriya Patel,
stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.
